note: Tier-3 generic passthrough adapter for the Gemini CLI (spawn-gemini.sh, the same instantiation shape as the Aider worked example, issue #4780). worktreeIsolation is declared 'no' EXPLICITLY, not 'partial' -- it is flatly unverified, not 'close but gapped'. This refuses Builder and Doctor (both require worktreeIsolation) and Judge (requires loomControl) by the same mechanism that already keeps Codex's 'partial' out of Builder; check-runtime-capabilities.sh needed no code change to enforce this. No guardrail-parity document exists or is required for tier-3 -- see defaults/docs/runtime-adapters.md's tier-3 section for why that is safe. Intended use: a #8436 runtimes.preference fall-through tap (claude -> gemini) for roles with no runtimeRequirements, so an exhausted Claude token pool does not strand continuous roles. Promotion to tier-2 requires a guardrail-parity document, a CI smoke leg, and an honest re-declaration of capabilities. Unattended pins in launch.extraArgs: --yolo auto-accepts every tool call (headless dispatch has no operator to answer gemini's approval prompts); --skip-trust trusts the dispatch worktree for the session (a fresh loom worktree has never been trusted and headless mode has no TTY to answer the prompt). Model mapping is deliberately NOT pinned: Loom's logical tiers (sonnet, opus, ...) are Claude names gemini does not understand, so no modelFlag is declared and LOOM_MODEL is dropped; gemini runs on its own default model, and an operator who needs a specific one passes --model through as a passthrough arg.
